earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only classification/wordlist refs (Bennett 1983; Boyd & Pasch 1988; Shimizu 1979); no grammar or phonology of Rang (Nigeria) found.

new_statements.quote: 12.1. Three level tones, High, Mid, Low are found in all the dialects studied, and usually they correspond without change. It is, therefore, necessary to postulate these three tones for Proto-Mumuye. A fourth tone, High to Low Fall, has been recorded in many of the dialects. The position for this tone in Proto-Mumuye is not clear. [p.52:] Concerning Rang and Pangseng, their separate tribal status directly corresponds to the fact that they also stand on their own linguistically.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Rang, like every Mumuye lect Shimizu compared, is a register-tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) and a HL falling tone in many dialects (a LH rise noted in a few items, fn. 23, p.68). The source makes no statement of any kind about word stress or accent: full-text queries for stress, accent, intonation and pitch return zero hits in this volume and stress returns zero across all of Shimizu's Mumuye volumes.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonal notes only (fourth tone HL fall not in all dialects; sporadic tonal changes, sec. 12.2).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about lexical tone on wordlist items (citation forms) across 14 Mumuye lects; the Rang wordlist is one of them. Snippet-only access: surrounding page text not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Rang is language-level in Glottolog (rang1269, ISO rax) but every source treats it as the Mumuye lect of Lamma: Wikipedia calls it a Mumuye clan of Lamma ward (citing Shimizu 1979: 13-19), Blench's Atlas (entry 394) classes it under 'Mumuye subgroup' with Shimizu 1979 as the only reference, and Shimizu 1979 p.52 says Rang and Pangseng 'stand on their own linguistically' among the 14 Mumuye lects he compared. The quoted tone statement is a blanket statement over 'all the dialects studied' in that comparative study (Rang included), not a Rang-specific description; the nearest full description is of the Zing dialect of Mumuye (Shimizu 1983; Glottolog nucl1240 folder holds its snippets). Zing Mumuye 'Ràn' = Lama inhabitants (Shimizu 1983 dictionary snippet).
